key_insight: Learned models predict high-quality QAOA angles in a single forward pass, replacing costly per-instance optimization with near-identical solution quality.
engineering_relevance: Repeated optimization of similar problems could amortize model training costs while accelerating the classical angle-selection step of hybrid quantum workflows.
method: Learn a mapping from problem instances to QAOA angles.
Use topology-sensitive models to improve angle quality.
Replace per-instance angle optimization with model inference.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports inference several orders of magnitude faster than the solver, generalization to unseen Barabási–Albert and 2D grid topologies, and quantum-hardware samples indistinguishable from those using solver angles.
watch_item: Up-front data generation and training costs must be amortized, and generalization beyond the evaluated problem distributions remains uncertain.
paper_title: Learning angles for quantum approximate optimization
